deposits.notes: Identified as an unverified lead in candidates.json, then independently found by DataCite title/author searches and OSF title/author searches; found_by=search because neither the saved paper nor the screening form names this deposit. The public node is titled Data for Hybrid Human–AI Societies Balance Creativity and Diversity. DataCite identifies it as IsSupplementTo https://osf.io/wzh2x, and the PsyArXiv preprint API links directly to node ku9cj. Anonymous GET requests returned HTTP 200 for the node, the osfstorage root listing, the Data and Code folder listing, and children. The root contains five files plus one folder, the folder contains eight files, and there are zero child components; n_files=13 counts repository files, not archive members. Both listings have no next page. README.md, storydata.ipynb, demographics.ipynb, statistics.ipynb, StoryData.zip, Experiment1.zip, and Experiment2.zip downloaded with HTTP 200; all data inspection stayed in memory. rows_checked=1875 is the combined row count of StoryData/Human.csv, StoryData/Mixed.csv, and StoryData/GPT.csv (625 rows each), not a human participant count. columns_checked lists their shared 43 columns. All 1875 rows have nonempty answer text, a participant_id, a unique node_id within condition, complete=True, failed=False, generation in 1-25, and a human_rating in 1-5. source is Human, Mix, or GPT and identifies network condition. Each file has 625 unique participant_id values, but numeric IDs overlap between files, so use a composite condition/source plus participant_id key. In Mixed.csv, time_taken>0 identifies 254 distinct human writers and time_taken=0 identifies 371 AI stories, as documented in README.md and demographics.ipynb. Human.csv has 625 positive-time human writers; GPT.csv has 625 zero-time AI records. The human storytelling analysis therefore contains 879 distinct condition-scoped human IDs. All 879 human stories have human_rating and text. Raw Experiment1 tables were also inspected. Human-only/CustomTrial_filtered.csv has 626 rows, Human-only/CustomTrial.csv 746, Human-AI/CustomTrial.csv 731, and AI-only/CustomTrial.csv 625. Following the notebook rule of retaining the last row per node_id yields 625 retained nodes in each condition; every prepared participant_id/answer pair was found in its corresponding raw retained table. Human-only/Participant.csv has 798 rows and Human-AI/Participant.csv has 418 rows; these are exported recruitment records, not analyzed counts. Node metadata files have 650 rows per condition and include id, degree, network_id, definition, and parent_id. S2 maps to deposit Experiment2, which provides individual rater rows rather than only aggregates. StoryTrial.csv rows by deployment are 3009 (2024-12-24), 480 (2024-12-27), 750 (2024-12-27-2), and 300 (2025-01-06). Unique rater IDs within those deployments are 108, 16, 25, and 10, respectively; these must not be added as verified globally unique people. Numeric answer ratings range from 1 to 5; the main deployment has 2998 numeric ratings, of which 2995 are nonfailed. The other deployments have 480, 750, and 300 nonfailed numeric ratings. The main raw rater-file columns are ["_initial_assets", "vars", "id", "creation_time", "failed", "failed_reason", "time_of_death", "type", "origin_id", "network_id", "complete", "node_id", "participant_id", "module_state_id", "trial_maker_id", "definition", "finalized", "is_repeat_trial", "score", "performance_reward", "parent_trial_id", "answer", "propagate_failure", "response_id", "repeat_trial_index", "n_repeat_trials", "time_taken", "time_credit_before_trial", "time_credit_after_trial", "time_credit_from_trial", "progress_before_trial", "progress_after_trial", "async_post_trial_required", "async_post_trial_requested", "async_post_trial_complete", "async_post_trial_failed", "block_position", "block", "class", "object_type", "rating", "source", "story", "text_color"]. In these raw rating files participant_id identifies the rater, story holds the stimulus text, source gives its network condition, and answer is the human score; join source/story to source/answer in the writing data to identify its writer. The prepared human_rating is a selected human rating per story, not an average over all raters: storydata.ipynb selects the first valid rating in a condition-dependent deployment order. It can draw on Experiment2 and June 2025 validation batches. The separate rating column contains GPT-judge scores. The raw rating files allow alternative per-story averaging and analysis-specific rater counts. Version limitation: the saved document is arXiv v3 dated 13 May 2025, whereas this deposit describes an expanded 2026 manuscript with 1473 humans and 8590 AI agents. The retained S1 counts match the saved paper, but the current S2 deployment has 108 rater IDs and 3009 trial rows; it does not by itself establish the exact saved-version 100-rater methods sample or 94-rater figure sample. Later validation ratings must not be silently treated as the original S2 sample. Experiment3-6 archives and remaining prepared CSVs are listed but their data were not inspected for this form, which contains only S1/S2. Experiment4.zip is 20680202 bytes and was not downloaded under the 20 MB limit. Public condition labels confirm arm membership, not random assignment between network compositions.

notes: Checked 2026-10-09. Read the entire saved markdown (252 lines, 37139 characters), including all references; the PDF has eight pages and no appendix or supplemental section. PDF text was checked on pp. 1, 3, 4, and 6, and all eight pages were checked for embedded URI links (none). The saved paper has no explicit data/code availability statement, preregistration link, repository link, or offer to provide data on request. The statements above preserve the source markdown verbatim for its printed task materials and software-framework reference; these are not claims that study data were deposited. The only printed web addresses are www.prolific.com (PDF p. 3 footnote 1) and www.psynet.dev (p. 4 footnote 2). https://www.prolific.com returned HTTP 200; https://www.psynet.dev returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to https://psynetdev.gitlab.io/PsyNet/. They are a recruitment platform and general experimental-software documentation, not additional study-data deposits. data_and_code.data_url and code_url in the form are empty. Public landing-page checks: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17962v3 returned HTTP 200 without a study-data/supplement repository link; https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/wzh2x_v1 returned HTTP 200 at https://osf.io/wzh2x_v1; https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/wzh2x_v1/ also returned HTTP 200. The OSF pages serve a JavaScript shell, so public API metadata was checked. The PsyArXiv metadata at https://api.osf.io/v2/preprints/wzh2x_v1/ (HTTP 200) states under both why_no_data and why_no_prereg: "All experiment and analysis code, as well as the human and AI data will be avilable upon publication.". This belongs to the 2026 preprint landing metadata, not the saved 2025 paper, and current anonymous file downloads demonstrate that the linked deposit is now public. The data DOI https://doi.org/10.17605/osf.io/ku9cj returned HTTP 200 at the same project; it is not a second deposit. The form has no final key or final.open_items, so what_we_could_compute is null instead of inventing an item-by-item mapping. Verified capabilities nevertheless include S1 writer-level creativity scores; arm-specific means, SDs, and descriptive SEs for 625 Human-only writers versus 254 human writers in Human-AI; analyzed writer/output counts and recruitment-versus-retained counts; and text-based diversity levels and changes across the 25 generations, including human-only subsets of the hybrid network. Individual S2 ratings can support per-story/rater averages and counts after an explicit inclusion rule. Network and generation dependence must be considered for inferential SEs, and the exact S2 sample and rating selection for the saved version remain unconfirmed. High confidence refers to public data availability and the inspected S1 columns/counts, not complete replication of the saved-version statistics. No account, access request, or authentication was used.
